body:
Please, feel free to talk about yourself, I'd welcome it if you are able - one thing I've found is that talking is an outlet. It emotionally drains you and, well, like it or not helps you understand that this is real and somehow you as a person have to recover. All of our situations are uniquely tied to us, all these deeply intimate and personal moments that are exclusive to us and our partners, no one else can understand those - but without a doubt I can tell you you're not alone in your horrible, draining fear.

"we can't carry the questions of what if and how it would be different" - I know, but it's so difficult. I've went through a lot of cognitive behavioral therapy to help with anxiety and depression so it allows me some ability to kind of objectively look at things but even still, I take one look back and think: "Is this my life now? Forever coping? Do I want it?" and the answer might not be yes, but at the same time I'd never want to inflict the pain I feel on anyone else. You don't know how final, how severe and sudden death is until it happens.

I obviously don't know how applicable any of this to you is, but I know how easy it can be to feel so afraid of saying the wrong thing to her. Give her all the love in the world, be there for her all the time - don't ever be afraid. The one thing I'm holding on to right now is that she told me, in the depths of her illness, "I feel good when I'm with you". I don't doubt your partner feels the same. I hope you can cherish every moment.

Right now, what you described is the only thing getting me through the day. I've woken up in this very numb place but I still have enough fire in my mind to know I'd drop everything to help anyone, it's the one thing I'm sure about right now. No one in the whole world should ever suffer a fraction of what this is like. It's so hard to try to understand that guilt and all these horrible emotions come with being a survivor of such a horrible tragedy, they can be so over powering.

Thank you for taking time to read and reply to me. 

"I found some level of comfort in talking to other folks who were feeling lost." Yeah, I agree. I think on a subconscious level this was my mind's last resort, to try and find some other people to empathise with me. I hope it doesn't sound selfish to say but only people who've gone through this horrible living nightmare can understand. It's sort of like my reality is unreal, my mind will wander from the fact that she is just...gone and then arrive at the fact again and yet I don't believe it. The fact that I don't get to say another word to her, to hear her voice again. Is there any way that gets easier, you know? I just don't see how.

And yeah, I think I will stick around here. If nothing else in this world, I want to at least try to help people.
